Using the corrected value \(2xy=\frac{7}{25}\):

\[
(x-y)^2=x^2+y^2-2xy=1-\frac{7}{25}=\frac{18}{25},
\]
so
\[
|x-y|=\frac{3\sqrt2}{5}.
\]

Since \(\alpha+\frac\pi4\in(\frac\pi2,\pi)\) and \(\sin(\alpha+\frac\pi4)=\frac45\), we get \(\alpha\in(\frac\pi4,\frac\pi2)\), hence \(\sin\alpha>\cos\alpha>0\). Thus

\[
\sin\alpha-\cos\alpha=\frac{3\sqrt2}{5}.
\]

Also

\[
\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha=\frac{4\sqrt2}{5}.
\]

Solving:

\[
\sin\alpha=\frac{7\sqrt2}{10},\qquad \cos\alpha=\frac{\sqrt2}{10}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\tan\alpha=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}=7.
\]

\[
\boxed{7}
\]
